Integrated multi-omics identifies distinct immune signatures with diagnostic and therapeutic implications in immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced myocarditis
articles.abstract: Abstract Immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis (ICI-myocarditis) is a rare but frequently fatal immune-related adverse event. A comprehensive understanding of the cellular and molecular determinants driving ICI-myocarditis is essential for improving diagnostic precision and developing targeted interventions. We delineate the immune landscape of ICI-myocarditis via scRNA-seq, flow cytometry, Olink proteomics, and multiplex cytokine profiling. We demonstrate that high levels of baseline ISG15⁺CD8⁺ T cells are linked to the proinflammatory features of monocytes and in vitro experiments confirm the existence of circulating ISG15⁺CD8⁺ T cells with a high potential to induce cardiomyocyte apoptosis, supporting their pathogenic potential for cardiomyocyte cytotoxicity. Notably, intercellular crosstalk between these subsets is possibly mediated via the CCL2-CCR2 axis, and its blockade attenuated ICI-induced cardiac injury in vivo. Based on the inflammatory signature in ICI-myocarditis, we develop an 8-protein custom panel with promising performance in distinguishing ICI-myocarditis from other ICIs-treated controls. JAK-STAT pathway activation promotes inflammatory programs in both ISG15⁺CD8⁺ T cells and monocytes. Furthermore, JAK-STAT inhibition ameliorates cardiac dysfunction and inflammatory infiltration while enhancing the response to anti-PD-1 therapy in mouse models. In summary, this study implicates immune-pathogenic features of ICI-myocarditis and provides a possible basis for future therapies.

articles.title:
Ice
Converts Phenols
into Persistent Mineral-Bound
Polymers
articles.abstract: Abstract Freezing fundamentally alters how minerals transform dissolved phenols in cold environments. As water freezes, solutes are excluded from the crystal lattice and concentrated into microscopic pockets of unfrozen liquid, creating reaction conditions far more extreme than those of bulk solution. Here, we compare catechol oxidation on a key soil manganese oxide under freeze–thaw versus room-temperature conditions. Freezing redirects products from soluble humic-like substances to thermally stable, mineral-bound polymers. Freeze–thaw conditions removed over 50% of dissolved organic carbon within 24 h compared to less than 10% at room temperature, with solid-phase carbon increasing over 50-fold. The attenuation of the effect with increasing salinity is consistent with freeze-concentration as a key driver and indicates that the pathway should be strongest in freshwater and low-salinity frozen environments. Freeze–thaw conditions also converted preformed soluble products into mineral-bound forms, demonstrating that the process operates on a range of substrates. These findings reveal an unrecognized abiotic carbon stabilization pathway that could operate when microbial decomposition is suppressed by freezing with direct implications for carbon dynamics in permafrost and seasonally frozen environments.

articles.title:
Why
Can Cross-End Point Transfer Fail in Computational
Toxicology? Diagnosing Decision-Structure Incompatibility across 13
End Points under Scaffold-Held-Out Evaluation
articles.abstract: Abstract Cross-end point information sharing may improve toxicity prediction when labeled data are limited, but biologically related end points are not necessarily predictively compatible. We evaluated transfer strategies across 13 toxicity end points using scaffold-disjoint repeated cross-validation with strict leakage control. The benchmark compared data-level pooling with higher-level approaches, including stacking, multitask learning, model-agnostic meta-learning, and frozen-encoder feature augmentation (FEFA). Direct cross-prediction between different end points was generally weak, with a mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC) of 0.525 across 156 ordered end point pairs, indicating limited standalone portability of end point-specific decision rules. Global data merging reduced macro-average ROC-AUC by 0.0287 relative to end point-specific baselines, whereas several higher-level approaches produced modest gains. The strongest macro-average improvements were observed for stacking (+0.0101 ROC-AUC) and FEFA (+0.0070), although effects varied substantially among end points. Additional decision-structure and representation analyses were consistent with transfer performance being strategy- and target-dependent rather than determined by biological relatedness alone. These findings support leakage-controlled, end point-specific evaluation when using cross-end point learning for chemical toxicity assessment and caution against indiscriminate pooling of heterogeneous toxicity data.

articles.title:
Decadal Biochar
Legacy Stabilizes Paddy Soil Carbon
by Reshaping Redox-Driven Reactive Oxygen Species Dynamics
articles.abstract: Abstract Biochar (BC) displays great potential in stabilizing soil organic carbon, yet its decadal legacy for carbon preservation under redox oscillations remains unclear. The study comprehensively investigated how decadal BC (D-BC) application restrained carbon mineralization of paddy soil via reshaping reactive oxygen species (ROS) dynamics. In situ fluorescence imaging and quantification results showed that D-BC soil inhibited hydroxyl radical (•OH) generation by 22.3% than fresh BC (F-BC) input soil, but elevating hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) and superoxide (O2•–) accumulation by 36.2% and 25.4% during redox oscillation, respectively. This resulted from its weakened microbial iron reduction and the lower reactivity of Fe(II), which significantly limited Fenton reactions. In contrast, a shift in the microbial community to redox-adapted taxa, lower catalase activity, and enriched dissolved inorganic carbon collectively facilitated the biogenic origin of H2O2 in D-BC soil. Scavenging and correlation analyses revealed that reduced •OH generation led to net suppression in CO2 emission from D-BC soil by >30% via upregulating the enzymatic latch, while enhanced H2O2 accumulation imposed oxidative stress on carbon-degrading microbes. Laboratory verifications confirmed the roles of surface oxidation and persistent free radical attenuation of aged BC in ROS redistribution. The failure of decadal straw (D-Straw) return to reproduce these phenomena suggested that the decadal BC legacy stemmed from a particular redox impact, rather than exogenous carbon input alone. The findings uncovered a new mechanism of BC-induced carbon stability, advancing understanding of the carbon cycle within redox-dynamic zones.

articles.title: Epitaxial-strain engineering of supported tensile noble metallene oxides for enhanced oxidation catalysis
articles.abstract: Abstract Supported two-dimensional noble metal oxides (metallene oxides) hold great promise for heterogeneous catalysis owing to their maximized surface exposure and tunable electronic structures. However, their high surface energy and low oxidation potentials make them intrinsically unstable under reaction conditions. Here, we report an epitaxial strain strategy to stabilize and modulate the electronic structure of supported PtO 2 metallene oxide. By employing rutile TiO 2 and rutile SnO 2 supports with distinct lattice parameters, we achieve epitaxial growth of PtO 2 metallene oxide layers with controlled strain states, where the larger-lattice SnO 2 substrate imposes biaxial tensile strain on PtO 2 . The tensile-strained PtO 2 /SnO 2 exhibits a reconfigured Pt–O electronic environment that simultaneously improves structural resilience and enhances the intrinsic reactivity of PtO 2 , delivering markedly improved methane oxidation performance with a T 90 of 370 °C (versus 434 °C for PtO 2 /TiO 2 and 469 °C for PtO x /Al 2 O 3 ) and <1% conversion loss over 38 h under both dry and wet conditions. Moreover, this epitaxial strain strategy is generalizable to other environmentally relevant oxidation reactions and rutile-type noble metal oxides, establishing tensile strain imposed by epitaxial lattice matching as a general principle for stabilizing atomically thin noble metal oxides while tuning their electronic structure.

articles.title: Current aviation roadmaps are not within planetary boundaries
articles.abstract: Abstract Aviation decarbonization roadmaps predominantly rely on replacing fossil kerosene with alternative jet fuels, yet the systemic impact of these alternatives on planetary boundaries other than climate change has not been quantified. Here we integrate prospective life-cycle inventories with the planetary boundaries framework to evaluate the absolute impacts of aviation roadmaps as time-dependent trajectories, rather than endpoint snapshots. Across scenarios to 2050, we find that fuel-switch-centered roadmaps do not achieve sustainability, persistently transgress the climate change and biosphere integrity core boundaries, and exert large demands for energy, land, freshwater and CO 2 capture that challenge their feasibility. Slower traffic growth brings aviation closer to its share of the safe operating space in terms of lowering energy demand, but respecting additional planetary boundaries requires air traffic to decline by at least 7.2% yr −1 . Our results show that aligning aviation with Earth’s safe operating space cannot be achieved through fuel substitution alone and requires governance strategies that combine supply-side solutions with explicit demand-side measures.

articles.title: Precise construction of antiparallel-stacked 2D imine covalent organic frameworks for atmospheric water harvesting
Multi-day recalibration-free electrophysiology interface based on carbon nanotube thin film dry electrodes
articles.abstract: Abstract Electrophysiological signals provide crucial and reliable information for decoding behavioral and cognitive human states. However, existing electrode interfaces are susceptible to artifacts or drift over time, thereby requiring frequent machine-learning model retraining. Here we present an end-to-end design of dry electrodes based on carbon nanotube (CNT) thin films, synthesized by a roll-to-roll floating catalyst chemical vapor deposition process. By balancing structural and electrical properties, we achieved low electrode-skin impedance, high signal fidelity, minimal motion artifacts, high breathability, and biocompatibility, outperforming the gold standard wet electrodes. In a multichannel myoelectric interface demonstration, these CNT electrodes maintained stable signals and consistent task performance across 14 days using only minutes of training data and no further model retraining. To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of a multi-day recalibration-free dry electrode system under naturalistic conditions, achieved by stable electrode–skin interface, rather than ongoing algorithmic adaptation.

articles.title: Wireless, optoelectronic, multimodal skin sensor for simultaneous monitoring of mechanical stress and vascular responses
CD200+ fibroblasts prime the immunoregulatory function of granulocytic myeloid-derived suppressor cells in inflammatory arthritis
articles.abstract: Abstract Granulocytic myeloid-derived suppressor cells (G-MDSCs) are immunoregulatory cells of the neutrophil lineage. Here, we show that immunoregulation by G-MDSCs is imprinted by the joint tissue microenvironment in patients with axial spondyloarthritis and in animal models of inflammatory arthritis. We demonstrate that the suppressive function of G-MDSCs is significantly enhanced in the joint tissue, but not in the circulation. Analysis of public single-cell RNA sequencing datasets was consistent with Cd200r1 high Hmgb2 + precursors differentiating into G-MDSCs following interaction with Cd200 + fibroblasts. In hTNFtg/ Il23mc mice, treatment with a CD200R1 agonist promoted an immunoregulatory signature associated with PD-L1 expression, whereas CD200 blockade reversed the phenotype. Following adoptive transfer of G-MDSC precursor cells into arthritic mice, administration of a CD200-blocking antibody impaired the differentiation of PD-L1 + G-MDSCs and exacerbated disease severity. These findings reveal a tissue-intrinsic program that facilitates resolution of inflammation through fibroblast-myeloid crosstalk that enhances G-MDSC function.

articles.title: Colossal visible birefringence and ultraviolet hyperbolicity in wide bandgap semiconductor CuAlO2
Population-resolved single-emitter spectroscopy
Disrupting the NAD+/NAM metabolic ratio driven by IL-1β inflammatory response potentiates chemotherapy and chemoimmunotherapy in mice
Mitochondria-localized circRNA BRAKE restrains adipogenesis under nutrient overload by disrupting ATP synthase assembly in mice
articles.abstract: Abstract Impaired adipogenesis contributes to obesity-associated metabolic disorders, in which mitochondrial dysfunction plays an important role. Emerging evidence suggests that mitochondria-localized circular RNAs (circRNAs) influence mitochondrial function; however, whether they regulate adipogenesis and systemic metabolism is unclear. By profiling circRNAs in mitochondria isolated from the white adipose tissue (WAT) of obese male mice, we observe an upregulation of Birc6 -circRNA Repressing Adipogenesis and Krebs-cycle Energy (BRAKE) in mitochondria. In vivo, adipocyte-specific circRNA BRAKE knockdown in male mice reduces body weight, restricts fat expansion, and improves insulin sensitivity. In vitro studies show that circRNA BRAKE inhibits adipogenesis. Mechanistically, circRNA BRAKE binds ATP5A and disrupts ATP synthase assembly, thereby reducing ATP production and mTORC1 signaling and suppressing adipogenesis. In omental WAT (oWAT) of patients with obesity, mitochondrial circRNA BRAKE levels are elevated and inversely correlated with mitochondrial bioenergetic function. Collectively, our data identify a mitochondria-localized circRNA that regulates energy metabolism and adipogenesis, suggesting that circRNA BRAKE may represent a potential therapeutic target for obesity-related metabolic diseases.

Reinforcement learning guided robotic platform that investigates and discovers asymmetric reactions
articles.abstract: Abstract Autonomous robotic platforms accelerate chemical discovery by coupling automated experimentation with algorithmic decision-making, but most lack integrated support for chirality and the sequential decision-making required to explore asymmetric reaction spaces with unknown reactivity and stereochemical outcomes. Here, we report a bespoke robotic platform guided by deep reinforcement learning that autonomously navigates a defined asymmetric reaction space by scouting reaction conditions, discovering chiral products, screening catalysts and mapping substrate scope. The structure-agnostic workflow is enabled by a digital twin of asymmetric catalysis, in which control policies are trained before transfer to the laboratory. We validate the approach in chiral phosphoric acid catalysis: over 30 days, the system made more than 3,000 decisions and uncovered four highly enantioselective transformations, including an axially chiral molecule and three allene syntheses, one involving the enantioselective functionalization of a pyrrolopyrrole moiety. These results highlight deep reinforcement learning-guided autonomy as a strategy for discovery in complex catalytic systems.

articles.title: Scellmate enables contamination aware curation and host mobilome linkage analysis of large SAG datasets

Selective Destabilization
of Mineral-Protected Organic
Carbon Accompanies Iron Reduction across a Coastal Wetland Salinity
Gradient
articles.abstract: Abstract Climate-driven seawater intrusion is intensifying salinization in coastal wetlands, but its consequences for the stability of sediment organic carbon (OC) remain poorly constrained. Here, we combined field observations along a natural salinity gradient with spectroscopic and mineralogical analyses, mineral sorption–desorption experiments, and manipulative incubations to examine the stability of mineral-protected OC. Salt-marsh sediments contained 9.23% less OC than freshwater sediments, with a disproportionate difference in reactive iron-bound OC (FeR-OC). Across the 36 independent field plots, FeR-OC represented 9.80–22.95% of total OC, while the FW–SM FeR-OC difference was numerically equivalent to 64.28% of the corresponding bulk-OC difference. This disproportionate response was associated with a shift from reactive Fe(III)-bearing phases toward Fe(II)-rich products, as well as a weakening of mineral protection, supported by spectroscopic, mineralogical, and geochemical evidence. In salt-marsh incubations, molybdate addition decreased FeR-OC mobilization by 39.51%, identifying a molybdate-sensitive contribution consistent with the sulfate-reduction branch. Together, these results support an iron-unlocking pathway in sulfate-rich coastal wetlands, in which Fe reduction weakens mineral protection and mobilizes previously stabilized OC. This mechanism identifies iron-mediated mineral protection as an important geochemical vulnerability of blue carbon under increasing seawater influence, while the subsequent mineralization, export, or recapture of mobilized OC remains unresolved.

articles.title:
Catalyst
or Bystander? Disentangling True Catalytic
Effects from Confounding Phenomena in Ozone-Based Wastewater Treatment
articles.abstract: Abstract Heterogeneous catalytic ozonation has generated thousands of publications over two decades, with these publications articulating a consistent narrative: catalysts enhance ozone decomposition, generate hydroxyl radicals (or other reactive species), and improve contaminant removal beyond that achievable by use of ozone alone. Despite this narrative, performance gains demonstrated at laboratory scale are routinely inconsistent and poorly reproduced at pilot and industrial scale. This perspective argues that the field suffers from a systematic attribution problem with observed enhancements frequently misattributed to catalytic activity when, instead, they arise from gas–liquid mass transfer modification, pH effects, and/or metal leaching driving homogeneous reactions. Using quantitative modeling, we further demonstrate that faster catalyst-mediated reaction kinetics alone may not translate into meaningful process-level benefits, particularly in full-scale reactors where relatively long hydraulic retention times and constraints on O3 gas–liquid mass transfer can diminish the advantage of kinetic acceleration. A sustained catalytic advantage at scale, therefore, requires not only kinetic acceleration but also more efficient utilization of ozone, an important distinction that has received limited attention in the HCO literature. Based on these findings, we propose a framework that will assist in distinguishing true catalytic pathways from various confounders and will help establish process-relevant benefit of HCO at scale. Overall, this perspective establishes a more rigorous evidentiary basis for translating catalytic activity into reliable wastewater treatment performance.

articles.title: Issue Editorial Masthead

Volatile and Semi-volatile
Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl
Substances (PFAS): Air–Water Partitioning, Atmospheric Emissions,
and Environmental Fate and Transport
articles.abstract: Abstract Volatile and semi-volatile per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (V/SV-PFAS) represent a class of PFAS that can partition into the gas phase, enabling atmospheric transport and inhalation exposure pathways that remain poorly understood. Recognizing that air–water partitioning is a fundamental determinant of environmental volatility, this review critically evaluates the current understanding of air–water partitioning coefficients (Kaw), atmospheric emissions, and subsurface occurrence and associated vapor intrusion (VI) risks of V/SV-PFAS. Experimentally determined Kaw values are compiled, highlighting variability spanning multiple orders of magnitude and uncertainties that may arise from limitations of conventional measurement techniques or differences in experimental methodologies. Recent advances, such as thermodynamic cycle methods, are assessed for their potential to expand the range of measurable V/SV-PFAS. Field observations from major atmospheric emission sources, including landfills, wastewater treatment plants, PFAS manufacturing facilities, vadose-zone soil gas at contaminated sites, and indoor environments, are evaluated. Fluorotelomer alcohols dominate V/SV-PFAS profiles, with concentrations of up to 105–106 ng/m3 in landfill and soil gas, 103–104 ng/m3 in industrial indoor air, 103–104 pg/m3 in ambient air near source regions, and 103 to 106 pg/m3 in indoor environments. Addressing critical knowledge gaps in air–water partitioning, source characterization, and subsurface fate and transport is essential for improving V/SV-PFAS exposure assessment and developing effective management strategies.

articles.title: Inland Migration Space Requirements for Maintaining Blue Carbon Stocks after Spartina Eradication under Accelerating Sea Level Rise
articles.abstract: Abstract China’s nationwide Spartina alterniflora eradication program across 18,000 km of coastline aims to restore native biodiversity, but removing these carbon-rich invasive stands is estimated to release 21.4 Mt CO2. This challenge is compounded by accelerating sea level rise, which threatens the native replacements meant to restore blue carbon functions, and current restoration approaches lack systematic strategies to address both pressures. We coupled species distribution modeling with the Sea Level Affecting Marshes Model (SLAMM) to project the performance of two posteradication restoration strategies─Environmental Suitability (ES, prioritizing habitat preferences) and Optimized Carbon Stock (CS, prioritizing high-carbon species)─under SSP1–2.6 and SSP5–8.5 through 2100, and quantified the minimum inland migration area required to sustain a target carbon stock (2.16 Tg C). Across projections for 2060 and 2100, tidal marshes outside seawalls are projected to lose 23–50% of their area, with carbon stocks declining 12–51% relative to 2021 levels. The CS strategy maintained 6–16% higher carbon stocks than ES. Mainting the target carbon stock required 31–157 km2 of inland migration space, with CS’s advantage over ES in reducing migration requirements narrowing from 37% under SSP1-2.6 (2060) to 4% under SSP5-8.5 (2100). These results show that management strategies lose effectiveness under extreme climate conditions, underscoring the value of early intervention under low-emission scenarios, and offer practical migration-space targets for coastal planning wherever invasive species control intersects with accelerating environmental change.

articles.title:
Fate
of Perfluoroalkyl Acids during Thermal Regeneration
of Hydrotalcite
articles.abstract: Abstract Calcined hydrotalcite (cgHT) is a promising PFAS adsorbent because it may enable PFAS destruction and sorbent regeneration at reduced temperatures. This study evaluated the thermal behavior of PFOS and PFOA adsorbed on cgHT at temperatures ranging from 125 to 550 °C and compared it with their behavior on sand (a reference carrier). Targeted PFAS, total fluorine, and fluoride analyses were used to quantify fluorine-containing products and establish fluorine mass balances across the solid, liquid, and gas phases. For both PFOS and PFOA, more than 75% of the initial fluorine remained associated with cgHT in an unextractable, likely inorganic form. In contrast, less than 40% of the initial fluorine was recovered as fluoride overall from the sand experiments, with less than 6% retained as solid-phase fluoride. Fewer types of volatile organic fluorine byproducts were detected in the cgHT experiments than in the sand experiments. Enhanced PFOS and PFOA degradation on cgHT may involve reactions with the bentonite binder, or the magnesium oxide and water generated from cgHT at elevated temperature. Adsorption and thermal regeneration performance did not change significantly over three adsorption–regeneration cycles. The results support further evaluation of cgHT as a thermally regenerable PFAS sorbent.

articles.title: Issue Publication Information

Putting Large Language
Models into Environmental Context
articles.abstract: Abstract The emergence of large language models (LLMs) has fundamentally transformed information interaction, yet their application in environmental science and engineering (ESE) is hindered by multimodal data formats, dynamic context requirements, and hallucination risks. To transition from general-purpose models to domain expert agentic systems, this Perspective introduces a three-pillar framework for ESE-LLMs: domain perception, knowledge grounding, and action capability. Implementing these capabilities introduces potential pitfalls such as geographic representation bias, catastrophic forgetting, and source authenticity vulnerabilities, which require strategic model blending and careful data curation to overcome. Furthermore, rigorous evaluation must extend beyond standard knowledge benchmarks to systematically assess factuality, fairness, consistency, and safety using both human and automated metrics. Finally, we present a decision-guided deployment workflow that helps researchers in ESE fields integrate LLMs into their workflow. Ultimately, achieving trustworthy environmental intelligence relies on continuous evaluation, robust governance, and sustained interdisciplinary collaboration to safely deploy agentic ESE-LLMs for high-stakes environmental challenges.

articles.title:
A Call to Future-Proof
Environmental Science and Engineering

Perturbation of
the Reproductive Endocrine System
by Halogenated Nitrophenols via Thyroid Receptor Signaling: Implications
for Developmental, Fertility, and Intergenerational Risks in Japanese
Medaka
articles.abstract: Abstract Disinfection byproducts (DBPs) are ubiquitously formed in disinfected drinking water and wastewater effluents, with emerging aromatic DBPs constituting a large fraction and generally exhibiting higher toxicity than regulated species. However, their ecological risks remain poorly understood. Here, we focused on two typical halogenated nitrophenols, 2,6-dibromo-4-nitrophenol (2,6-DB-4-NP) and 2,6-dichloro-4-nitrophenol (2,6-DC-4-NP), and systematically evaluated their developmental and reproductive toxicity in Japanese medaka at environmentally relevant ng/L concentrations. Early-life exposure significantly delayed hatching and increased larval mortality, while a 110-day chronic exposure inhibited further gonadal development. These effects were linked to disruption of thyroid hormone homeostasis, reflected by an altered triiodothyronine/thyroxine (T3/T4) ratio and dysfunction of the hypothalamic–pituitary–thyroid (HPT) axis, which subsequently led to sex-specific dysregulation of the hypothalamic–pituitary–gonadal (HPG) axis. Males displayed elevated estrogen levels, enhanced estrogen receptor signaling, and hepatic vitellogenin synthesis, whereas females showed the opposite pattern, indicating a feminization risk and diminished estrogenic responses, respectively. Furthermore, parental exposure caused developmental impairments in the offspring, suggesting potential intergenerational toxicity. In silico docking further revealed that 14 other aromatic DBPs exhibited high-affinity binding to thyroid hormone receptors (TRα and TRβ), similar to the two halogenated nitrophenols, supporting their potential to disrupt TR-mediated signaling. Collectively, this study adds to the limited in vivo evidence of thyroid and reproductive endocrine disruption by halogenated nitrophenols under environmentally realistic conditions, underscoring their ecological significance and implicating TR signaling as a mechanistic node for future study.

articles.title:
Associations of
Early Pregnancy Contaminant Exposure
with Gestational Diabetes Mellitus and Mediation by Metabolic Pathway
Perturbations
articles.abstract: Abstract Early pregnancy exposure to environmental contaminants is a known risk factor for gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), yet the metabolic pathways linking specific chemical categories to disease pathogenesis remain largely unknown. To address this gap, we conducted a meet-in-the-middle mediation analysis within a prospective birth cohort, leveraging a nested case–control study (116 GDM cases, 232 controls) with 182 contaminants across 11 chemical categories and 702 metabolites measured in early pregnancy serum samples. Seven individual contaminants showed significant associations with GDM risk, with BHT-COOH exhibiting the strongest effect (OR = 2.34, 95% CI: 1.59–3.45). Weighted quantile sum (WQS) regression indicated a positive mixture association with GDM, with Bayesian kernel machine regression (BKMR) providing a complementary assessment of mixture effects. Notably, we identified 506 exposure–metabolite pairs with significant mediation and consistent directionality, providing a comprehensive profile of candidate metabolic intermediates in the associations between contaminant exposure and GDM. Pathway-level analysis identified six candidate metabolic pathways with significant mediation effects, among which the phenylalanine, tyrosine and tryptophan biosynthesis pathway showed the largest mediation estimate, accounting for 75.5% of the DEHP/DNOP–GDM association. Similar pathway-level mediation effects were observed for both individual contaminants and the mixture exposure index. Collectively, these findings identify potential metabolic intermediates linking early pregnancy contaminant exposure to GDM and provide hypotheses for further epidemiological and experimental validation.

articles.title:
Data-Driven Accelerated
Design-Synthesis of Heterogeneous
Fenton-like Catalysts for Water Decontamination
articles.abstract: Abstract Heterogeneous Fenton-like catalysis offers an effective approach for organic pollutant removal, yet catalyst development remains largely empirical and lacks a closed-loop design-synthesis-validation framework. Here, we report a synthesis-oriented inverse-design framework for Fe-based catalysts. We first developed ML_Removal to predict pollutant removal, achieving a test-set R2 of 0.970, while SHAP analysis identified specific surface area (SSA) and Fe loading (Fe wt %) as actionable catalyst descriptors. We then built two synthesis-to-property models to predict SSA and Fe wt %, with SMOTER augmentation enhancing model performance and yielding test-set R2 of 0.782 and 0.856, respectively. Coupling these models with NSGA-II enabled the identification of candidate synthesis recipes targeting the SSA and Fe wt % windows. Two catalysts synthesized according to the NSGA-II-derived recipes exhibited measured SSA of 538.40 and 468.63 m2/g and Fe wt % of 8.19 and 7.01 wt %, aligning with the design targets. The catalysts achieved broad pollutant removal, retained activity in real waters matrices, and maintained >71% naproxen removal after five cycles. External validation of ML_Removal using the experimental data sets yielded an R2 of 0.784, demonstrating transferability to pollutants absent from the training set. Overall, this work establishes a closed-loop design–synthesis–validation framework for data-driven catalyst development and experimental realization.

articles.title:
Microbial
Degradation of Lignin Generates Iron-Binding
Organic Ligands
articles.abstract: Abstract The association of organic carbon (OC) with iron (Fe) minerals is a primary mechanism governing soil OC persistence, yet the molecular agents mediating Fe–OC binding remain poorly defined. In this study, we demonstrated that microbial degradation of lignin, one of the major contributors to soil OC, generates organic compounds with the potential to bind to Fe, with implications for mineral-associated carbon stabilization. Lignin samples were microbially degraded by Pseudomonas putida KT2440 for 30 days and subsequently reacted with FeCl3. Ultrahigh-performance liquid chromatography–high-resolution tandem mass spectrometry (UHPLC–HRMS/MS)-based analysis identified 494 distinct molecular features with MS/MS data, of which 21 were identified as lignin-derived Fe-binding ligands using Fe isotopologue-enabled metabolomics. Structural annotation of 15 identified ligands further elucidated the chemical nature of the lignin-derived compounds. Systematic meta-analysis of more than 20,000 public HRMS datasets revealed that related compounds occur in soil and aquatic organic matter across diverse ecosystems, ranging from grassland to Arctic tundra. Ion identity molecular networking (IIMN) further revealed additional putative ligands and structurally related transformation products. Altogether, our findings provide a molecular framework for investigating how microbially generated Fe-binding ligands may contribute to Fe–OC interactions and potentially, soil carbon stabilization under changing climate conditions.

articles.title:
Fusion-DeepRSM
for Satellite-Derived PM2.5 Estimation and Precursor Sensitivity
Prediction
articles.abstract: Abstract Accurate estimation of fine particulate matter (PM2.5) and characterization of precursor-response relationships are crucial for human health protection and air quality management. However, current approaches remain limited by the high computational cost and uncertainties of chemical transport models (CTMs), as well as the sample imbalance and limited interpretability of observation-based machine learning methods. Here, we developed Fusion-DeepRSM, an observation-constrained extension of the Deep Learning Response Surface Model (DeepRSM) framework that integrates CTM simulations, multisource satellite observations, and ground-based measurements to derive spatially continuous PM2.5 concentrations and characterize precursor-PM2.5 response relationships. Results from ground-based observations and CTM-based testbed experiments show that Fusion-DeepRSM effectively alleviates the sample imbalance in conventional models and mitigates PM2.5 overestimation in rural regions, with an average reduction of 4.13 μg/m3 while maintaining high predictive accuracy (R2 = 0.872 and RMSE = 11.82 μg/m3). In addition, Fusion-DeepRSM successfully quantifies precursor-PM2.5 response relationships, revealing pronounced seasonal and regional heterogeneity consistent with established atmospheric chemistry understanding. With high computational efficiency, Fusion-DeepRSM further quantifies the effects of meteorological conditions and pollutant concentrations on PM2.5 variability. During the nationwide PM2.5 decline from 2020 to 2023, unfavorable meteorology partially offset pollutant-related improvements (+1.2 versus −1.8 μg/m3), while changes in precursor pollutant conditions played an important role in the February 2023 PM2.5 rebound in the Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei region. These findings demonstrate the strong potential of Fusion-DeepRSM for air quality modeling and region-specific pollution mitigation.

articles.title:
Covering
and Flaring Manure Storage Units as a Methane
Mitigation Strategy for Small- to Midsize Dairy Operations in the
United States
articles.abstract: Abstract Covering manure storages and flaring the captured methane (cap-and-flare) offers a technically feasible mitigation pathway for small- and midsize dairies that has received limited attention relative to anaerobic digestion (AD). While AD systems are more economically feasible for large operations, the dairy segment with fewer than 1,000 cows still produces approximately 34% of U.S. milk and remains largely unaddressed. We estimated technical CH4 mitigation potential under full cap-and-flare adoption using the IPCC Tier 2 model for 8,675 dairy farms across 38 US states. Under 100% adoption, liquid storage CH4 mitigation potential (GWP100 = 27) ranged from 5.53 MMT CO2e yr–1 (central 90% interval: 3.70–6.63) to 10.36 (central 90% interval: 6.93–12.42) depending on the Arrhenius activation energy and reference temperature constants applied, representing 16–30% of the CO2e attributed to dairy manure CH4 in the 2022 EPA Greenhouse Gas Inventory. These values represent an upper-bound technical potential rather than a projected deployment level. Average national Levelized Costs of Mitigation (LCOM) ranged from $55 t–1 CO2e (conservative parametrization) to $29 t–1 CO2e (upper-bound parametrization), positioning cap-and-flare as a cost-efficient CH4 mitigation option. Existing USDA-NRCS Conservation Practice Standard 367 provides an available incentive mechanism, although meaningful scale-up will likely require dedicated funding for infrastructure and technical assistance. These results suggest that cap-and-flare could complement AD as a mitigation pathway for U.S. dairy operations where AD is not economically viable.

articles.title:
Greenhouse Gas and
Ammonia Emission Factors from Raw
and Digested Cattle Slurry: A Field-Based Synthesis for Cattle Systems
articles.abstract: Abstract Anaerobic digestion (AD) of cattle slurry is widely promoted as a manure-management strategy, yet its effects on greenhouse gas (GHG) and ammonia (NH3) emissions remain uncertain. This review provides the first field-based synthesis of paired methane (CH4), nitrous oxide (N2O), and NH3 emission factors (EFs) from raw and digested cattle slurry during storage and land application. A total of 98 paired observations from 16 studies were analyzed using paired bootstrap geometric mean ratios. AD reduced dry matter, volatile solids, and carbon content while increasing total ammoniacal nitrogen (TAN) and pH. Consequently, digestate CH4 EFs during storage were 51% lower than those of raw slurry (p = 0.001). In contrast, NH3–N EFs increased by 63% during storage (p = 0.071) and by 40% following land application (p = 0.003). However, TAN-normalized NH3 EFs did not differ between manure types, suggesting similar volatilization potential. AD had no significant effect on N2O EFs. A system-level analysis showed that AD reduced total GHG emissions across the storage-to-land-application continuum by 49%, although this benefit was partially offset by increased NH3 losses. These findings identify AD as an effective CH4 mitigation strategy for cattle slurry when combined with targeted NH3 abatement measures to maximize environmental benefits.
